question_text: Connect the following (exhaustive): Sachin Tendulkar, 2011; Gagan Narang, 2012; Mary Kom, 2013.
answer_text: Each of them waved the chequered flag to start the Indian Grand Prix in the year listed (Sachin Tendulkar did so in 2011, pictured waving the chequered flag at the Indian Grand Prix).

question_text: Connect the following (non-exhaustive): Raabta - Agent Vinod; Galla Goodiyan - Dil Dhadakne Do; Chale Jaise Hawaein - Main Hoon Na; Sexy Baliye - Secret Superstar; Barson ke Baad - Anjam.
answer_text: Bollywood songs with a single-shot (one continuous take) video sequence.

question_text: A tweet from Netflix India (@NetflixIndia), posted 9:34 AM, 29 October 2021, reads: 'Not trying to be [a word blurred out] but Tweeting to let you know The Social Network is currently streaming.' What is the occasion or context of this tweet?
answer_text: Facebook's rebranding to Meta (announced 28 October 2021). Netflix India was referencing the film The Social Network (about Facebook's founding) to mark the occasion, with the blurred word presumably being 'Facebook'.

question_text: The Tangaliya is a 700-year-old indigenous weavecraft native to a community of a historical region in X. Extra yarns in contrasting colours are knotted around the yarns of the fabric during weaving to create embossed bead-like patterns, visible on both sides of the fabric. It's a craft not known to be practiced anywhere else in the world and has been accorded GI status. The Tangaliya weave came into the limelight in 2025 when the protagonist of a major Hollywood movie (Y) was seen sporting a piece of clothing made from it during an iconic late re-entry scene and in some promo events. It was again in the news recently when a major sports team from X wore it on X's founding day. Identify X (5) and Y (5).
answer_text: X = Gujarat (the Tangaliya weave belongs to the Dangasia community of Saurashtra, Gujarat; the Gujarat Titans IPL team wore Tangaliya shirts on Gujarat Diwas). Y = F1 (The Movie) - Brad Pitt's character wore a Tangaliya weave shirt.

question_text: Sunfeast is ITC's food brand, largely known for biscuits, pasta and instant noodle variants. In November 2023, the Sunfeast Yippee range of noodles launched a new flavour called '____ Masala'. The name ____ was perhaps chosen not just to convey the feeling the masala would leave one with, but also to capitalise on a Delhi personality making headlines around that time, to the point that celebrities like Deepika Padukone were also seen posting social media content in recognition of that personality's achievements. Fill in the blank and give the funda / identify the personality.
answer_text: WOW Masala - named after Jasleen Kaur's viral catchphrase 'So beautiful, so elegant, just looking like a wow.'

question_text: In 1985, Jordan Mechner used a handheld Bolex camera to shoot videos of his brother David running, jumping, and climbing walls and ledges at their high school parking lot, which he processed using specialised equipment. 39 years later, they revisited the campus to recreate the video when Jordan was publishing a book about his work. Jordan credits David's physical prowess and agility as one of the biggest contributors to his work and its success. Give the funda - what did Jordan do with this footage?
answer_text: Jordan Mechner used the footage of his brother's movements as reference (rotoscoping) to animate the character for his video game Prince of Persia.

question_text: In 1807, William Cobbett wrote a story about using a 'device' as a child, though there was no evidence of its effectiveness or even its actual use - in fact, Mythbusters episode 148 busted the alleged utility of this device. Cobbett's story was a critique of the British press's indulgence in publishing unverified news (misreporting Napoleon's defeat in this instance). Though references to the use of this device existed before Cobbett's story, it is his reference that is credited with popularising it - one that most of us have thoughtfully used, and sometimes effectively. Identify the device.
answer_text: The 'red herring' - from Cobbett's story about dragging a red herring tied to a string to draw hunting hounds (harriers) off the trail of a hare, giving rise to the idiom for a misleading distraction.

question_text: Christine Roussell, aunt of Academy Award winner Melissa Leo (The Fighter, 2010), is an art historian, curator and conservator who has worked at the Met, been involved in the conservation of the Statue of Liberty, and is considered an authority on art in New York City. Having previously authored a book on a NY icon's art, in continuation of a similar related role, she authored a book titled '_____ __ _ _____: The Making of an American Photograph', investigating the story behind an iconic photograph that was in fact a staged PR exercise rather than a spontaneous moment, aimed at reviving optimism. Fill in the blank / give the funda.
answer_text: 'Lunch Atop a Skyscraper: The Making of an American Photograph' - about the famous 1932 photograph of construction workers eating lunch on a steel beam high above New York City (also known as 'Lunch on a Beam').

question_text: Born in 1895 in Lahore, this man earned his Bachelor of Accountancy from Aligarh Muslim University before joining the Indian Railway Accounts Service in 1920. For his services to British India he was appointed a Companion of the Order of the Indian Empire in 1941, and received knighthood in the 1946 King's Birthday Honours List. After Partition he opted for Pakistan and was handpicked by Muhammad Ali Jinnah as Pakistan's first Finance Minister, presenting its first budget, drafting its first Five-Year Plan, overseeing creation of the State Bank of Pakistan, and later serving as the third Governor-General of Pakistan (1951-1955). When he departed for Pakistan, he also left behind a company he had helped establish in 1945 with two brothers from Ludhiana - Jagdish and Kailash - who promptly renamed the company, partly to reflect their Indian identity and partly to save on rebranding costs. What was the name of the company?
answer_text: Mahindra and Mohammed - renamed to Mahindra and Mahindra (the man was Sir Ghulam Mohammed).

question_text: What hereditary title do they all share (exhaustive)? 1. Hasan Ali Shah Mahallati [1817-1881]; 2. Shah Ali Shah [1881-1885]; 3. Sir Sultan Mohammed Shah [1885-1957]; 4. Prince Shah Karim Al-Hussaini [1957-2025]; 5. Prince Shah Rahim Al-Hussaini [2025-present].
answer_text: Aga Khan - the hereditary title of the Imam of the Nizari Ismaili Muslims.

question_text: In 1969, this Oscar-winning actor played a driver chasing the Indianapolis 500 in the film Winning. The role planted a lifelong obsession and he continued to be a competitive racer until age 81. Around the time Winning was filmed, his wife bought him a Rolex chronograph (ref. 6239) at Tiffany & Co., its caseback engraved 'DRIVE CAREFULLY ME.' He wore it almost daily for the next 16 years, single-handedly turning a commercial flop into the most coveted chronograph in watch-collecting history. On 26 October 2017, that watch sold at auction in New York for $17.8 million, a record at the time. What is the model name of this Rolex watch, which owes its popularity to this American actor, befitting his racing obsession and an iconic win in Florida at age 70 in 1995?
answer_text: The Rolex Daytona 'Paul Newman' (Paul Newman Daytona).

question_text: X was a British singer born in New Delhi in 1941 to expat parents. After independence his parents moved to Darjeeling to manage tea estates until X's father's death in 1954, when X moved to London. X and his two siblings started a band called the Saints before each pursued solo careers; his siblings had their own hit tracks 'Well I Ask You' and 'My Resistance Is Low'. X himself had a chart-topping song (A) in 1969, essentially a romantic novel in song form about a fictional woman named Marie-Claire who rises from poverty in the back streets of Naples to join European high society, name-dropping the Boulevard St Michel, the Sorbonne, the Aga Khan, Sacha Distel, Juan-les-Pins and St Moritz. This was X's only major chart-topper. Song A found a second life when it was featured in a 2007 movie. Name the 1969 song and the 2007 movie (5 each).
answer_text: Song: 'Where Do You Go To (My Lovely)' by Peter Sarstedt. Movie: The Darjeeling Limited (2007, directed by Wes Anderson).

question_text: In the summer of 1976, as the United States celebrated a milestone anniversary, a fraternal organisation of military veterans gathered in Philadelphia for their 58th annual state convention. Roughly 2,000 attendees - mainly former servicemen who had fought in the World Wars - checked into the grand Bellevue-Stratford Hotel. Within days of returning home, attendees began falling ill with high fevers, chest pains and severe pneumonia. 182 people were sickened and 29 died. It wasn't until January 1977 that microbiologist Joseph McDade identified the culprit: a previously unknown rod-shaped bacterium thriving in the hotel's air conditioning cooling tower, spreading through the ventilation system as a contaminated mist. The bacterium was given a scientific name honouring the veterans' group, paired with a species name meaning 'lung-loving'. What is the common name of this illness, still contracted today from contaminated water systems in hotels, hospitals, cruise ships and hot tubs?
answer_text: Legionnaires' disease, caused by the bacterium Legionella pneumophila, named after the American Legion convention in Philadelphia, 1976.

question_text: Having immigrated to New York at age nine, this Dartmouth-educated entrepreneur and philosopher-investor is one of Silicon Valley's most prolific early-stage investors, with stakes in Uber, Twitter, Notion, Postmates, Yammer, OpenDNS and Stack Overflow, among hundreds of others. He became a cultural icon for blending Eastern philosophy with Silicon Valley capitalism, gaining a massive following through aphorism-laden tweets on wealth, happiness, leverage and specific knowledge, later compiled into a book. He has said: 'I was a totally unknown kid in New York City from a nothing family... Then I passed the test to get into Stuyvesant High School. That saved my life, because once I had the Stuyvesant brand, I got into an Ivy League college, which led me into tech... You go from being blue collar to white collar in one move.' Who are we talking about?
answer_text: Naval Ravikant (the book of his aphorisms is 'The Almanack of Naval Ravikant').

question_text: The following is a blog entry by an author (X) responding to a query about impostor syndrome with an anecdote: 'Some years ago, I was lucky enough to be invited to a gathering of great and good people: artists and scientists, writers and discoverers of things. And I felt that at any moment they would realise that I didn't qualify to be there, among these people who had really done things. On my second or third night there, I was standing at the back of the hall, while a musical entertainment happened, and I started talking to a very nice, polite, elderly gentleman about several things, including our shared first name* (Y). And then he pointed to the hall of people, and said words to the effect of, "I just look at all these people, and I think, what the heck am I doing here? They've made amazing things. I just went where I was sent." And I said, "Yes. But you were the first ___ __ ___ ____. I think that counts for something."' Identify X and Y (5 each).
answer_text: X = Neil Gaiman (author of the blog entry). Y = Neil Armstrong (the elderly gentleman who shared the first name 'Neil'); Gaiman told him 'you were the first man on the moon.'

question_text: On 04.01.2019, Chris Godfrey set out to do something and achieved it in 10 days, creating history. In doing so, he joined an elite list which reads as follows: Justin Bieber - 2012; Justin Bieber - 2013; Justin Bieber - 2014; Kim Kardashian - 2015; Justin Bieber - 2016; Selena Gomez - 2016; Beyonce - 2017; Kylie Jenner - 2018. For 1436 days, Chris's achievement was unparalleled, and it was only in December 2022 that history was created again, surpassing his achievement in less than 2 days. What did Chris Godfrey do?
answer_text: Chris Godfrey created the 'World Record Egg' Instagram post (@world_record_egg, posted 4 January 2019), which in 10 days became the most-liked photo on Instagram, surpassing Kylie Jenner's post (18 million likes). It held the record for 1436 days until it was beaten by Lionel Messi's World Cup winning celebration post on 18 December 2022.

question_text: Tie-Breaker 1: Images shown are a close-up of white crochet/lace fabric, an airplane seat with embroidered headrest covers, and a map of the South Sulawesi region of Indonesia (highlighting the Makassar area). What connects these images to Alexander Rowland, an 18th-century London barber?
answer_text: Macassar Oil - Antimacassar. Alexander Rowland made a hair pomade called Macassar Oil, made from the oil of Macassar Ebony, a tree native to Macassar (Makassar) in Indonesia, used to slick back men's hair. The oil stained furniture, leading women to create embroidered protective cloth covers called 'antimacassars', which were used on sofas and eventually carriages and airplane seats (as shown in the images).

question_text: Tie-Breaker 2: The following is the manufacturing journey of a brand's product, a cumulative 50,570 miles travelled for a specialised client. Materials: USA - Clay; New Zealand - Wool; UK - Felt weaving; China - Petroleum Naphthalene; South Korea - Sulphur; Japan - Magnesium Carbonate; Greece - Silica; Thailand - Zinc Oxide; Philippines - Glue; Malaysia - Rubber; Philippines - Rubber. Production: Philippines. Packaging: Indonesia. Client Destination: X. Identify X.
answer_text: X = Wimbledon (the All England Lawn Tennis Club). The journey describes the manufacturing of Slazenger's Wimbledon tennis balls, with the final destination leg of 6,660 miles to Wimbledon.
